title: Fact-generated interpreter VM — Deegen two-tier paper alignment
north_star: A fully-proven, correctness-verified JS VM (test262/Node-oracle backed) that reaches V8-comparable performance on the real v8-v7 (Octane-derived) benchmark suite -- not a curriculum proxy -- with minimal RSS, achieved entirely through general, workload-shape-justified architecture (fact-generated interpreter, region-stencil baseline JIT, tier-switching, generic IC, a proven cycle collector, provably-scoped arenas) and ZERO benchmark-specific cheating of any kind: no code path may detect a benchmark's name, file, fixture identity, or shape and special-case it; every optimization admitted anywhere in this codebase must be justified by a runtime-shape argument that generalizes to any JavaScript program with that shape, verified against the neutral corpus AND the deegen-curriculum AND the v8-v7 suite together, never tuned to move one benchmark's number in isolation. See docs/benchmark-integrity.md for the mechanical detail; this is the plain-language statement of why that document's rules exist.
constraints: quench-runtime owns JavaScript semantics; quench-node owns only the Node host boundary
Benchmark fixtures and workload-specific kernels are not production VM semantics

No benchmark cheating, stated plainly: production code must never special-case a specific benchmark file, function name, fixture identity, or known input shape from richards.js/deltablue.js/splay.js/etc (or any curriculum/micros case). If a change only helps because it recognizes which program is running, it is disallowed regardless of the score improvement -- see the north_star field above and docs/benchmark-integrity.md.
Every fact is Proven, Guarded, or Unknown; every fast path (interpreter, IC, JIT) has complete fallback semantics
Generated code is derived from one declaration; handwritten code is limited to irreducible behavior
Every task belongs to exactly one theme

Performance measurements are evidence: any optimization admitted here must generalize to any JavaScript program with the same runtime shape, not be sized to one fixture's numbers (see docs/benchmark-integrity.md)

Deegen (arXiv:2411.11469) is a two-tier design: interpreter + baseline JIT + tier-switching. No optimizing JIT, no deoptimization protocol — the paper doesn't build either. See docs/deegen-alignment.md.

Tasks 027-037 closed with task 037's own recorded finding that the status-table closure gate was NOT fully satisfied (Optimizing-tier net win unproven, tag register blocked, hot-cold splitting not justified -- all three confounded by the x86_64-only executable gate on this ARM64 dev machine, see docs/deegen-alignment.md). Tasks 039+ are the direct, in-backlog continuation addressing that finding, not new scope creep. No fixture-specific tuning (e.g. Splay/Richards helpers) or performance work OUTSIDE this deegen_full_jit theme starts until this theme's own task chain is done.
The existing ExecutionTier::Optimizing scaffold is kept as a beyond-paper extra optimization layer, not described as the paper's (nonexistent) optimizing tier

deegen_full_jit.goal: Complete quench's alignment with the Deegen paper's (arXiv:2411.11469) actual two-tier design, per the audited gap table in docs/deegen-alignment.md. Tasks 027-044 are closed (034 and 043 with applicability findings). External research (2026-09) found IC/stencil-coverage refinement has a well-documented diminishing return versus true speculative optimization, which this project has correctly and permanently decided not to build (see docs/deegen-alignment.md). Tasks 045-047 are now closed profile-gated no-go findings: their required measurements did not justify a shared cache, rope representation, or frame-pooling change. Remaining work is 048-049, still bounded and fallback-complete.

vm_completeness.goal: Beyond Deegen-paper alignment: what a top-level JS VM needs that the deegen_full_jit theme never covered, discovered while trying to run the v8-v7 (Octane-derived) benchmark suite for a real V8-comparison score. Task 050 is fixed and task 051 is closed with a finding: the reported Splay mismatch was a stale timing-score harness comparison, not a VM tree-semantics divergence. Task 052's tracked runner is landed and its 300-second ARM64 release ground-truth row now verifies all eight fixtures. Then survey three genuinely uncovered areas by any prior task: regex engine performance (053), TypedArray fast-path coverage (054), and allocation-throughput for allocation-heavy workloads (055) -- all profile-gated, same discipline as 045-047. Task 056 now has measured evidence of pure-Rc cycle retention in plain-object, closure, and DeltaBlue-shaped graphs; task 057 is therefore justified for the periodic full-pass cycle-collection implementation. NAMED TARGET, reverse-engineered from real numbers: the complete 300-second row is 71.84 geomean versus a ~60,000 target (Node's own local aggregate is 87,774.56), with RegExp's 1.59GiB peak RSS now explicit. Four tasks close the gap this session's investigation found NOT previously covered: 068 (highest leverage -- native ARM64 stencil execution is opt-in-only and currently a net loss when enabled, so tasks 039/040/042/048/049/058's work contributes zero to any measured score until this is fixed), 069 (Crypto has no owner among the 5 timing-out benchmarks), 070 (completed ground truth for all 8 benchmarks before 053/054/055/069's surveys work half-blind), 071 (attack the IC/layout-mismatch constant factor directly -- 062-067 prove the complexity class is sound, but Richards/DeltaBlue's ~1000x gap is a constant-factor problem 045/047's narrower closed questions didn't fully explain). Every one of 068-071 carries a mandatory anti-cheat validation section (synthetic generalization clone, grep for fixture-identity detection, cross-verification against the neutral corpus and curriculum, not just v8-v7) so gains are architectural, not benchmark-specific tuning.

architecture_invariants.goal: Prove the VM's foundational complexity claims hold via permanent cargo-test invariants (scaling behavior, never absolute wall-clock thresholds), subsystem by subsystem, BEFORE further tuning work proceeds in that subsystem -- flip the order from 'tune, then accidentally discover an architecture bug' (how the for-in quadratic scan, the property-write quadratic bug, and task 061's DeltaBlue finding all actually happened) to 'prove the foundation first, then tune with confidence.' 062 covers object/shape/property/call-dispatch/bytecode-dispatch (already in progress, invariant #1 passed). 063-067 extend the same technique to array/Map/Set, strings, closures/call-frames, raw allocation, and the JIT/stencil tier respectively. Tuning tasks in the other themes are wired to depend on their subsystem's invariant suite: 054 (TypedArray) on 063, 058 (shape hash-consing) on 062, 059 (arena) on 066, 048/049 (region growth) on 067. Every invariant must be validated to actually fail against a deliberately-introduced regression before being trusted to pass against the real implementation -- a loose bound defeats the purpose.
